reason: Both fully satisfy the hard requirements (correct headings/order, snapshot-first gating, no restart/failover before snapshot, and clear abort/rollback conditions in multiple phases), but Response B shows slightly sharper technical judgment — it distinguishes a necessary I/O freeze/quiesce from a restart (clarifying that snapshot consistency need not violate the no-restart rule), flags that VACUUM/compaction itself consumes I/O and can worsen the very latency problem being fixed, and explicitly warns against starting a second concurrent remediation before completing or reverting the first.
